content.title: Today is Ivy Day—the Day When High School Seniors Find Out if They Got Into an Ivy League School
content.text: Ivy DayCatherine McQueen - Getty ImagesEach spring, high seniors around the world who applied regular decision to an Ivy League university prepare themselves for Ivy Day, the moment when the schools simultaneously release their regular decision results. This year it falls on March 26, and students, families, and college admissions advisers are waiting by their computers for news.If recent acceptance trends are any predictor, most of those who applied will face either outright disappointment in the form of a rejection letter or continued suspense in the form of a notice that they’ve made the school’s wait-list. For the latter, that means they will have to put off offers from other schools (most require a deposit by May 1) in hopes they’ll receive good news from their top choice.Many education-world observers, faculty members, and students are not fans of Ivy Day as it places what many believe is unhealthy attention on an already fraught process. In an article this week in the Daily Princetonian titled “Abolish Ivy Day,” a student named Audrey Tan argued that Princeton should not release its decisions on the same day as other Ivies because simultaneous announcements can feel overwhelming. “When a student is receiving up to eight high-stakes decisions in the same day, they may not be able to separate and process each decision as they might had they come out as isolated decisions at distinct times.”One of the more taxing rituals of Ivy Day is the almost-constant toggle high schoolers and their families make from email inboxes to social media to see how their friends and acquaintances have fared. Amid all the Instagram reeling and Reddit posting, college admissions specialists, as well as etiquette experts, recommend that everyone try to remain calm.And if the results aren't in your favor, just know you're not alone. Last year, the overall admission rate at Harvard was 3.42 percent and at Yale it was 4.62 percent. (We'll update both schools’ numbers, as well as the other Ivies, with this year's numbers in the a.m.)You Might Also Like
